name: AI supply chain thematic equity
heading: The Structural Opportunity: AI Infrastructure Investment Cycle
caseLead: Growth in demand for AI computing supports investment across semiconductors, memory, networking, power equipment, cooling and data centres. Competition among major cloud providers and government support for domestic technology supply chains can sustain demand, although the pace of customer spending remains the main driver of supplier earnings.
caseRest: The strategy relies heavily on capital spending by a small group of major technology companies, so weaker investment plans can affect suppliers across the sector. Valuation risk compounds this exposure because expected growth is often priced several years ahead, making the basket sensitive to interest rates and evidence that customers are using capacity more efficiently. The indicative profile of 19.0% annual return, 31.0% volatility, a 55.0% worst fall and 0.1 return skew shows that strong long-term growth comes with large cyclical drawdowns.
figNote: Each card shows the percentage change in the PHLX Semiconductor Sector Index, or SOX, over the episode described. The SOX tracks major listed semiconductor companies and provides a consistent market measure of changing demand, earnings expectations and valuation across the AI supply chain.

events.title: Credit stress cuts technology investment
events.text: The financial crisis reduced technology orders as customers cut inventories and financing conditions tightened, taking the SOX 69% below its 2007 peak. The strategy lost because semiconductor earnings and valuation multiples fell together.

events.title: Huawei restrictions disrupt chip demand
events.text: US restrictions on Huawei increased the risk of lost sales and excess inventory across global semiconductor suppliers, pushing the SOX down about 16% during May. The strategy lost because China represented a major end market and manufacturing base.

events.title: Covid halts orders before cloud demand rises
events.text: The Covid sell-off initially reduced hardware orders and disrupted Asian manufacturing, taking the SOX about 35% below its February peak. The strategy lost because near-term demand and production fell before cloud investment and remote working supported recovery.

events.title: Chips Act supports domestic capacity
events.text: US approval of semiconductor subsidies improved the outlook for domestic fabrication, equipment and infrastructure investment as the SOX rose about 16% during July. The strategy gained because public support reduced the cost of expanding advanced manufacturing capacity.

events.title: Nvidia guidance confirms rapid AI spending
events.text: Nvidia’s revenue guidance showed that hyperscalers were accelerating purchases of AI processors and supporting systems, lifting the SOX about 15% during May. The strategy gained because stronger orders raised earnings expectations across chips, memory, networking and cooling.

events.title: DeepSeek challenges expected computing demand
events.text: DeepSeek’s efficient AI model raised concern that advanced systems might require less computing capacity, pushing the SOX down 9.2% on 27 January. The strategy lost because lower expected capital intensity reduced long-term revenue assumptions for infrastructure suppliers.

instrument: Global listed semiconductor, memory, networking, power, cooling and data-centre equities; rebalanced quarterly
rules: Companies require material AI infrastructure revenue, positive expected growth and adequate trading liquidity; exposure capped by company, industry and region
costs: Estimated bid-ask spreads, commissions, withholding taxes and quarterly rebalancing costs deducted
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from AI capital spending to diversified risk control

legs.purpose: Captures growth in AI computing capacity
Captures data transfer and storage demand

entry: Added at quarterly reviews when AI infrastructure revenue and order growth meet the portfolio thresholds
size: Company weights capped at 8%, industry weights at 40% and single-country exposure at 55%
exit: Removed when AI exposure falls below the threshold or forward orders decline for two consecutive quarters
stop: Basket exposure reduced when aggregate hyperscaler capital-spending guidance contracts year on year
marketWatch: Hyperscaler capital-spending guidance is the main indicator because it leads orders for processors, memory, networking equipment and power systems. Semiconductor inventories, data-centre power connections and supplier order backlogs show whether spending is reaching the wider supply chain. Earnings reports, export-control decisions and major AI model releases are the key upcoming events.

favourable.heading: Hyperscalers raise capital spending
favourable.text: Higher hyperscaler investment favours the strategy because processor purchases require additional memory, networking, power and cooling capacity. Nvidia’s May 2023 guidance confirmed this mechanism and lifted earnings expectations across the supply chain.

favourable.heading: Supply constraints support margins
favourable.text: Tight supply favours the strategy when strong demand allows component producers and equipment suppliers to raise prices and operate factories at high utilisation. The 2020 to 2021 chip shortage supported revenue growth and margins across several semiconductor segments.

favourable.heading: Industrial policy funds capacity
favourable.text: Public support favours the strategy because subsidies and tax credits lower the cost of new fabrication plants, power connections and domestic supply chains. US approval of the Chips Act in July 2022 improved the investment outlook for semiconductor equipment and construction suppliers.

adverse.heading: Capital spending guidance weakens
adverse.text: Lower hyperscaler guidance hurts the strategy because suppliers plan capacity against a small number of large customer budgets. The 2018 semiconductor downturn showed how weaker orders and inventory reductions can spread quickly from end customers to equipment and component producers.

adverse.heading: Export controls restrict sales
adverse.text: Tighter export controls hurt the strategy by reducing access to major customers and forcing suppliers to redesign products for regulated markets. US restrictions on Huawei in May 2019 lowered expected sales across semiconductor companies with substantial China exposure.

adverse.heading: Efficiency reduces computing needs
adverse.text: More efficient AI models hurt the strategy when investors reduce assumptions for processors, power use and data-centre construction. The January 2025 DeepSeek release produced this response because its reported training efficiency challenged expected capital intensity.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy’s estimated peak-to-trough return during each event using the sector weights, company caps and quarterly rebalancing rules above. Each event window runs from the last portfolio high before the shock to the subsequent low.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated return over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn’s scenario engine projects moves in semiconductor equities, data-centre suppliers, interest rates, energy prices and regional risk premiums, then applies them to the strategy’s sector and country exposures.
altTitle: Where Else Can Investors Find AI Growth?

related.why: Owns durable growth across industries and bears valuation risk rather than concentrated AI capital-spending risk.
Follows equity price trends and bears reversal risk instead of relying on infrastructure demand.
Owns regulated infrastructure and bears construction, inflation and policy risk while earning from capacity investment.
